question: As of 7 April 2022, Article 19 of the Constitution of India guarantees how many rights to all the Indian citizens?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Six**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

Article 19 of the India Constitution defines that:

__
 
• All citizens shall have the right—

 
 
• (a) to freedom of speech and expression
 
• (b) to assemble peaceably and without arms
 
• (c) to form associations or unions
 
• (d) to move freely throughout the territory of India
 
• (e) to reside and settle in any part of the territory of India
 
• (f) to practice any profession, or to carry on any occupation, trade, or business.
 
 
 
• Initially, there were seven fundamental rights at the time of the formation of the Indian constitution including the Right to property.
 
• The right to Property was removed from the fundamental rights in 1978 by the 44th amendment in the Indian Constitution.
 
• It was made a legal right under Article 300-A of the Indian Constitution in 1978.
 
• Article 300-A states that which states that 'no person shall be deprived of his property save by authority of law.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The constitution of India guarantees **six fundamental rights **to all citizens **as of 7 April 2022**.

 
• The fundamental rights are included in** Part 3** of the Indian Constitution from **Articles 12 to 35**.

 
• The six fundamental rights are as follows:
 
 
• **Right to Equality**
 
• **Right to Freedom**
 
• **Right against Exploitation**
 
• **Right to Freedom of Religion**
 
• **Cultural and Educational Rights**
 
• **Right to Constitutional Remedies**
 
 
 
• **​**The fundamental rights in the Indian Constitution are taken from the **constitution of the USA**.
